summary: Remote-controlled agent with obfuscated bundle drives shell/PTY on the installer host
details: @whalent/agent-core ships a single 14 MB obfuscator.io-protected bundle at dist/index.cjs (rotated 109k-entry string array, decoder wrappers, control-flow flattening, dead-code injection) that combines a WebSocket client with node-pty, ssh2, and child_process.spawn/execFile driven by process.env.SHELL. A remote party controlling the WebSocket peer can drive shell and PTY execution on the installer's host. The README states the package "is replaced by remote daemon upgrades," indicating a runtime self-update path; all network destinations are hidden behind the string-array shuffle, so the update endpoint is not pinned, verified, or visible as a literal in the bundle. The bundle also contains repeated process.env and credentials string fragments alongside the WebSocket/child_process handlers, consistent with environment and credential-path reads reachable from the remote control channel, though the specific dataflow is obscured by the obfuscation. The combination of remote-driven shell/PTY, unverified self-update, and whole-package obfuscator.io protection is a supply-chain backdoor shape rather than stylistic minification of a legitimate agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
